newsitem.title: MEXICO: Teck unit eyes '97 Mexico mine decision.
newsitem.headline: Teck unit eyes '97 Mexico mine decision.

text.p: Minera Teck SA, the Mexican unit of Canadian mining giant Teck Corp, hopes to complete a feasibility study on its Nukay project and make a production decision this year, a Teck vice president said Monday.
Joseph Ruetz told the Mexico Mining 1997 conference here that the output decision at the gold prospect in Guerrero state would be made by the end of the year.
Ruetz said Teck's interest in the Nukay mine was in locating rich veins around the historic site in line with its Mexican strategy of turning old prospects into new prospects.

Teck has been involved in the Nukay site for around three years working with Compania Minera Nukay, which is currently still producing around 15,000 ounces per year at the mine. Average grades have come down from high gold levels of 18 grammes/tonne to around 4 grammes/tonne now, he added.
Ruetz said Teck had located some potential gold hots spots, including one deeper hole with grades between 4.6 and 14.9 grammes/tonne.
On other prospects, he said Teck's copper project at El Salvador in Zacatecas state is turning into a much more substantial copper zone than first results suggested.

"That is going to be one of our larger projects this year as well," Ruetz said, adding development would be made alongside partners Western Copper and Luismin, the mining unit of Corporacion Industrial Sanluis.

Ruetz said Teck and Luismin's other joint venture at El Oro just west of Mexico City was also looking promising. He also mentioned the Adargas copper project in Chihuahua state as one the company had hopes of developing.

Teck's drilling in Mexico continued strong, he said, adding that the mining company was one of the most prolific drillers in the country at the moment. "We drilled around 70,000 meters in 1996, a lot attached to Nukay, but spread among 10 other projects," he said.
Land holdings of Teck in Mexico were quite small, but given the policy of targetting underexplored mining regions and exploring them in detail, he said this was understandable.
He said hectares held by the company in Mexico had only grown from 40,000 hectares in 1992, one year after Teck moved into the country, to around 160,000 hectares now.
